title: Transitivity $T_{F,\Qlb}\circ T_{E,F}\cong T_{E,\Qlb}$
statement:
For a prime $\ell$, a scheme $X$ and finite extensions $E\le F$ of $\mathbf Q_\ell$ inside
$\Qlb$, there is a natural isomorphism

$$
T_{F,\Qlb}\circ T_{E,F}\;\cong\;T_{E,\Qlb}\colon D(\Mod_{E_X})\longrightarrow
D(\Mod_{\overline{\mathbf Q}_{\ell,X}})
$$

between the derived extensions of scalars of [def-sfb-derived-extend-subfield] and
[def-sfb-derived-extend-to-qlbar].

proof.text: Put $\varphi:E_X\to F_X$, $\psi:F_X\to\overline{\mathbf Q}_{\ell,X}$, and $\chi:E_X\to\overline{\mathbf Q}_{\ell,X}$ for the coefficient inclusions underlying [def-sfb-derived-extend-subfield] and [def-sfb-derived-extend-to-qlbar]. Write $A=\operatorname{Ext}_{\varphi}$, $B=\operatorname{Ext}_{\psi}$ and $C=\operatorname{Ext}_{\chi}$. These functors are right exact by [sk-def-sfb-change-of-scalars](2). The functor $A$ preserves finite limits by [lem-sfb-subfield-flat]; $B$ and $C$ do so by [lem-sfb-qlbar-flat], applied to $F$ and to $E$, respectively. Thus all three are exact. These applications require only the stated finite subextensions and the arbitrary scheme $X$.

By the restriction formula in [sk-def-sfb-change-of-scalars](1), the $E_X$-action on $\operatorname{Res}_{\varphi}\operatorname{Res}_{\psi}N$ is $\gamma_N\circ(\psi\otimes\mathrm{id}_N)\circ(\varphi\otimes\mathrm{id}_N)=\gamma_N\circ((\psi\circ\varphi)\otimes\mathrm{id}_N)$. Restriction leaves underlying morphisms unchanged, so $\operatorname{Res}_{\varphi}\circ\operatorname{Res}_{\psi}=\operatorname{Res}_{\psi\circ\varphi}$ as functors. The adjunctions in clause (2) give, naturally in $M,N$,
$$\Hom(BAM,N)\cong\Hom(AM,\operatorname{Res}_{\psi}N)\cong\Hom(M,\operatorname{Res}_{\varphi}\operatorname{Res}_{\psi}N)=\Hom(M,\operatorname{Res}_{\psi\circ\varphi}N).$$
Consequently $B\circ A$ is left adjoint to $\operatorname{Res}_{\psi\circ\varphi}$.

The functor $\operatorname{Ext}_{\psi\circ\varphi}$ is also left adjoint to $\operatorname{Res}_{\psi\circ\varphi}$ by [sk-def-sfb-change-of-scalars](2). Apply the equal-right-adjoint case of [lem-weil-pbc-conjugate-iso-unit-equation] to the adjunction in step 2 and this adjunction; it gives the canonical unit-compatible natural isomorphism $B\circ A\cong\operatorname{Ext}_{\psi\circ\varphi}$. By [lem-sfb-subfield-coefficient-map-comp], $\psi\circ\varphi=\chi$; [def-sfb-extend-scalars-iso-of-eq] then gives the specified comparison $\theta:B\circ A\xrightarrow{\sim}C$.

The exact-functor clause of [sk-def-sfb-derived-categories], together with the definitions [def-sfb-derived-extend-subfield] and [def-sfb-derived-extend-to-qlbar], identifies $T_{E,F}\cong D(A)$, $T_{F,\Qlb}\cong D(B)$ and $T_{E,\Qlb}\cong D(C)$. For a cochain complex $K$, the maps $\theta_{K^n}:B(A(K^n))\to C(K^n)$ commute with differentials because $C(d_K^n)\theta_{K^n}=\theta_{K^{n+1}}BA(d_K^n)$, the naturality equation of $\theta$. They therefore define a natural chain isomorphism with inverse given by $\theta_{K^n}^{-1}$. For each of $A,B,C$, exactness preserves the kernels and cokernels defining cohomology, so $H^n(D(F)K)\cong F(H^n(K))$ for $F=A,B,C$; hence each functor sends quasi-isomorphisms to quasi-isomorphisms. The universal property of localization therefore sends the chain isomorphism and its inverse to mutually inverse natural transformations on derived categories. Applying $A$ and then $B$ termwise gives exactly the objects, differentials and maps of $B\circ A$ termwise. Thus
$$T_{F,\Qlb}\circ T_{E,F}\cong D(B)\circ D(A)\cong D(B\circ A)\xrightarrow{D(\theta)}D(C)\cong T_{E,\Qlb},$$
with source and target the unbounded derived categories in the statement.
